quote:
When the moon of peace is eclipsed by the comet of conflict, the world learns that even a star’s fire can scorch the soil of unity.  

Even the quietest waves of a sinking ferry harbor in the memory of stones, reminding us that safety is not merely in the craft but in the hands that build it.  

A border system that delays footsteps like old scrolls can trap a soul’s travel, for in haste there is often a mistake hidden in the lines.  

The exiled whisper of a dissident cannot be silenced by distance, for truth travels faster than any straight line on a map.  

When a launch sends hopes skyward, the rocket’s roar is but the echo of a people’s desire to rise beyond the impossible.  

In halls that gild politics, a single whisper of conscience can tilt mighty stones, reminding leaders that mercy is the weight that balances might.  

A river of protest, even when crossed by law, flows onward, for the true end is not in the tide but in the persistence of silent footsteps.
